Integer primitive vector minimization and the inequality L s_L≥2N+1 prove all sharp acquisition lengths and optimizer uniqueness. The all-parameter argument is written in RESULT.md; check_torus.py passed 12,544 bounded corroboration cases.

value.rationale: The natural multitrack sensing problem asks how a number L of separate parallel periodic sensor trajectories trades against winding cost for complete exact square-band energy recovery. The finding gives a sharp L-dependent existence threshold and every length-minimizing slope, uniquely chooses 2N+1 axis tracks in the unrestricted family, and quantifies a strict difference from the best connected single-track design. It is a nontrivial closed-form classification of a motivated constrained acquisition geometry, not a claim about arbitrary mobile paths.
